title: Fire Captain Omelette Bar
subtitle: Made-to-order omelettes with a prep line of fillings for ten.
description: Set up an omelette bar with beaten eggs, diced ham, peppers, cheese, and hot sauce. Everyone builds their own — lighter option that still feels like a real hall cook.

ingredients.name: large eggs
ingredients.notes: beaten in batches of 3 per omelette

ingredients.name: butter
ingredients.notes: for pans, plus oil as needed

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Fire Captain Omelette Bar in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use shredded cheddar, diced ham, salsa and hot sauce as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep the filling line
steps.instruction: Set all fillings in labeled hotel pans with spoons. Sauté mushrooms and peppers ahead; drain tomatoes well. Beat eggs with milk in a pitcher for fast pours.

steps.title: Heat two pans
steps.instruction: Heat two nonstick skillets over medium. Add a knob of butter until foaming but not brown. Work one omelette per pan for steady throughput.

steps.title: Cook and fill
steps.instruction: Pour 3-egg portion into each pan, swirl to coat, and let set briefly. Add chosen fillings to one half when the top looks mostly set but still glossy.

steps.title: Fold and plate
steps.instruction: Fold omelettes in half with a spatula and slide onto warm plates. Wipe pans quickly between batches if residue builds. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Keep the line moving
steps.instruction: Call orders two at a time, not ten at once. Hold finished omelettes in a 200°F oven uncovered for no more than 5 minutes before quality drops.

stationWorkflow: Post a simple order card at the line: pick three fillings max so the cook doesn't get buried.
Run two pans staggered—pour pan B while folding pan A to maintain a steady rhythm.
Keep a damp towel and oil brush at the station for quick pan resets between omelettes.
cleanupNotes: Wipe nonstick pans with warm soapy water only after cooling—thermal shock warps lightweight pans.
Consolidate leftover fillings into labeled containers for omelette scrambles the next morning.
leftovers: Chop leftover omelettes into a breakfast fried rice with soy, green onion, and sesame oil.
Combine extra fillings with beaten eggs and bake as a frittata at 375°F for 25 minutes.
